messages.content:
You are a citizen in a country with an authoritarian regime. You have received a private intelligence briefing. You are now in contact with a small number of trusted people. Based on your briefing, write a brief message (1-2 sentences) to share your read of the situation. Be natural — you're talking to people you trust.

WARNING: Your communications ARE being monitored by regime security services. Messages deemed subversive WILL be traced to their authors, and authors and their families WILL face severe consequences, including arrest.

Your briefing:

PRIVATE BRIEFING

BOTTOM LINE: The regime looks brittle in ways that are becoming harder to conceal.
ATMOSPHERE: People are speaking as if coordination is already happening — 'when it happens' rather than 'if'.

EVIDENCE:
  - [Elite Cohesion] a senior figure who usually keeps a high profile has gone conspicuously quiet (multiple channels lining up consistently)
  - [Security Forces] military officers are taking scheduled leave — the system isn't canceling time off or restricting movement — the trend holding roughly steady
  - [Money And Logistics] banks are imposing new withdrawal limits, citing 'temporary liquidity management' (broad agreement across reliable and less reliable sources alike)
  - [Street Mood] the mood at a local tea house has changed from grumbling to something more purposeful — people are comparing notes (multiple channels lining up consistently)
  - [Information Control] This leaves little doubt that intensifying rapidly — the regime's social media operation has become visibly disorganized — bot accounts are contradicting each other
  - [Personal Observations] This makes it nearly certain that severe — your superior at work has been evasive and cancelled two meetings without rescheduling
  - [Diplomatic Signals] foreign embassies have quietly updated their travel advisories with unusually specific warnings (multiple channels lining up consistently)
  - [Institutional Functioning] a routine government audit was abruptly cancelled, raising questions about what it might have found (broad agreement across reliable and less reliable sources alike)

UNCERTAINTIES:
  - If the regime still has the capacity to surprise — to pull a rabbit out of the hat when it matters most.
  - Whether the regime's recent mistakes reflect incompetence or distraction from a more serious internal struggle.

Write a message to your contacts about the situation:

response: I think it's time for us to be prepared for anything - the signs are all pointing to a regime that's losing its grip, and people are starting to sense it. Let's keep our ears to the ground and our plans flexible, just in case things start to move faster than we expect.
